content: 1. Drospirenone and Ivacaftor: Drospirenone may increase the levels of ivacaftor by influencing the metabolism mediated by the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. The clinical significance of this interaction is currently unknown. 2. Drospirenone and Ivosidenib: Drospirenone may elevate the levels or effects of ivosidenib through its impact on CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical relevance of this interaction remains unclear. 3. Drospirenone and Ixabepilone: Drospirenone may enhance the levels or effects of ixabepilone by altering CYP3A4-mediated metabolism. The significance of this interaction is uncertain. 4. Drospirenone and Ixazomib: Drospirenone may increase the levels or effects of ixazomib via modulation of CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical importance of this interaction is not well established. 5. Drospirenone and Juniper: Juniper may potentiate or interfere with the diuretic effects of drospirenone. While juniper has diuretic properties, high doses may lead to kidney damage. Close monitoring is advised. 6. Drospirenone and Ketamine: Drospirenone may increase the levels or effects of ketamine by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 7. Drospirenone and Ketoprofen: Both drospirenone and ketoprofen can increase serum potassium levels. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is recommended. 8. Drospirenone and Ketorolac: Drospirenone and ketorolac, including intranasal formulations, both elevate serum potassium levels. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are necessary. 9. Drospirenone and Labetalol: Both drospirenone and labetalol can increase serum potassium levels. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is advised. 10. Drospirenone and Lacosamide: Drospirenone may increase the levels or effects of lacosamide by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is uncertain. 11. Drospirenone and Lamotrigine: Drospirenone may reduce the levels or effects of lamotrigine by increasing hepatic clearance. Combination oral contraceptives, including drospirenone, have been shown to significantly decrease plasma concentrations of lamotrigine, likely due to induction of lamotrigine glucuronidation. Caution and monitoring are advised. 12. Drospirenone and Lansoprazole: Drospirenone may increase the levels or effects of lansoprazole by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical relevance of this interaction is unknown. 13. Drospirenone and Lapatinib: Drospirenone may elevate the levels or effects of lapatinib through CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unclear. 14. Drospirenone and Larotrectinib: Drospirenone may increase the levels or effects of larotrectinib by modulating CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical importance of this interaction is not well defined. 15. Drospirenone and Lemborexant: Drospirenone may enhance the levels or effects of lemborexant via CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is uncertain. 16. Drospirenone and Levalbuterol: Drospirenone increases serum potassium levels, while levalbuterol decreases it. The net effect of this interaction is unclear, so caution is advised. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are recommended. 17. Drospirenone and Levamlodipine: Drospirenone may increase the levels or effects of levamlodipine by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 18. Drospirenone and Levomilnacipran: Drospirenone may elevate the levels or effects of levomilnacipran through CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical relevance is uncertain. 19. Drospirenone and Levonorgestrel (Intrauterine and Oral): Drospirenone may increase the levels or effects of levonorgestrel (both intrauterine and oral formulations) by modulating CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is not well established. 20. Drospirenone and Linagliptin: Drospirenone may increase the levels or effects of linagliptin by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical importance is unclear. 21. Drospirenone and Liraglutide: Drospirenone may reduce the effects of liraglutide by altering passive renal tubular reabsorption due to increased pH. Caution and monitoring are advised. Oral contraceptives may also impair glucose tolerance, reducing the hypoglycemic effects of antidiabetic agents. Glycemic control should be closely monitored in diabetic patients. 22. Drospirenone and Lisinopril: Both drospirenone and lisinopril can increase serum potassium levels due to pharmacodynamic synergy. Caution and close monitoring are necessary to mitigate the risk of hyperkalemia. 23. Drospirenone and Lomitapide: Drospirenone may increase the levels of lomitapide by modulating CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 24. Drospirenone and Lonafarnib: Drospirenone may elevate the levels or effects of lonafarnib through CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical relevance is uncertain. 25. Drospirenone and Lonapegsomatropin: Drospirenone may reduce the levels or effects of lonapegsomatropin due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Oral estrogens may also reduce serum insulin-like growth factor-1 (IGF-1) response to growth hormone analogs, potentially necessitating higher growth hormone doses. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are recommended. 26. Drospirenone and Lopinavir: Drospirenone may increase the levels or effects of lopinavir by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unclear. 27. Drospirenone and Lorlatinib: Drospirenone may elevate the levels or effects of lorlatinib through CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical importance is not well defined. 28. Drospirenone and Lornoxicam: Both drospirenone and lornoxicam can increase serum potassium levels. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are necessary. 29. Drospirenone and Losartan: Drospirenone may increase the levels or effects of losartan by modulating CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs can also elevate serum potassium levels. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are advised. 30. Drospirenone and Lovastatin: Drospirenone may increase the levels or effects of lovastatin by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is uncertain.
